description: The Octameter Injection System is an aftermarket vapor injector that uses engine vacuum to draw a metered water/methanol mixture (Octamite Formula) from a reservoir, through an adjustable Barometric Altitude Selector and a 0.022-inch orifice, injecting the resulting vapor mist into the engine intake to supplement the air/fuel charge.

fitment.trim_note: Exempt for 1982 and older model-year gasoline and propane powered motor vehicles; no specific make/model is listed in the document.

notes: No part numbers or make/model fitment table appear anywhere in the document; the exemption applies generically to '1982 and older' gasoline and propane powered vehicles. Category is ambiguous under the fixed enum: the device is a vacuum-driven water/alcohol vapor injector that ties into the intake vacuum system rather than a traditional intake manifold or air filter/duct; classified as 'intake' as the closest fit ('other' would also be defensible). Executed date is a handwritten numeral on page 2 read as the 23rd day of September, 1982. Document includes a August 3, 1982 CARB staff report (pages 3-5), a device diagram (page 6, Figure 1), and a September 8, 1982 letter from EPM Industries (page 7, Attachment 2) as supporting attachments; these do not add any part numbers or vehicle fitment beyond what is stated in the Executive Order itself.
